name: Is this PDF to Word converter really free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, completely free. No subscription, no watermarks, no per-page limits. The entire conversion happens in your browser using open-source libraries.

name: Does my PDF get uploaded anywhere?

acceptedAnswer.text: Never. Your file is read by your browser locally. There is no server involved at any step of the conversion.

name: What is the difference between Text mode and Image mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Text mode extracts the text from your PDF and creates an editable Word document with paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, and tables. Image mode renders each page as a high-resolution image and places it in the Word document — the visual layout is preserved exactly but the text cannot be edited.

name: Will the formatting look the same in Word?

acceptedAnswer.text: In text mode, the text content and basic formatting (bold, italic, font size, headings, tables) are preserved. Complex multi-column layouts may not match exactly. For perfect layout fidelity, use image mode.

name: Can I convert a scanned PDF to Word?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your scanned PDF contains an embedded text layer (many modern scanners add one), text mode will extract it. If the PDF is image-only with no text layer, use image mode to get a Word document with page images, or use the OCR PDF tool first to add a text layer before converting.

PDFree detects tables in two ways: by aligning text items into columns (for data tables), and by detecting drawn border lines (for grid forms). Detected tables become proper Word tables — not plain text. Very complex or merged-cell layouts may not convert perfectly.

name: Do I need Microsoft Word to open the converted file?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The .docx format is supported by Microsoft Word, Google Docs (upload to Drive and open), LibreOffice Writer (free, open-source), and Apple Pages. You do not need a paid Microsoft 365 subscription to open the file.

name: What is the maximum file size for PDF to Word conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no hard limit. However, very large PDFs (100+ MB) may take longer and require more memory. For best results keep files under 100 MB in text mode and under 50 MB in image mode at 300 DPI.

name: How does the conversion quality score work?

acceptedAnswer.text: After converting, PDFree shows a confidence score (0–100%) based on what was detected in your document: text layer coverage, tables, diagrams, and script complexity. High (80%+) means fully editable output. Fair (55–79%) means some pages may be image-only. Limited (under 55%) usually means the PDF is mostly scanned — run OCR first for editable Word output.

name: Is there a PDF to Word converter that doesn't upload files?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — PDFree. The entire conversion runs inside your browser using PDF.js and WebAssembly. Your PDF is never sent to any server. You can verify this by opening DevTools → Network tab and watching that no file upload request is made during conversion. Most online converters upload your file to their servers; PDFree does not.

name: Does it support Arabic, Hebrew, Cyrillic, or Chinese text?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Text mode supports Latin, Cyrillic (Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian), Arabic and Hebrew (with correct right-to-left paragraph direction), CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), Devanagari (Hindi), and most Unicode scripts used in standard PDFs.
